stimuli.title: Lata, Pia, Tara, Charu, Aditi, Jaya, Uma, Farah occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Aditi occupies floor 1, flat A.
• The floor numbers of Tara and Uma differ by 1.
• Tara and Aditi live in different flat letters.
• Lata and Farah live in different flat letters.
• Lata lives below Pia.
• The floor numbers of Tara and Aditi differ by 3.
• Lata lives above Farah.
• Jaya and Uma live in different flat letters.
• The floor numbers of Charu and Aditi differ by 2.

Statements: No deposits is a loans. Some loans are coins. All coins are accounts.
Conclusions:
I. All deposits are accounts.
II. Some accounts are loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few deposits are loans. All loans are coins. No coins is a accounts.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are not loans.
II. No loans is a accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:

questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

Conclusions: I. V < U   II. T ≥ P.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings rural access = lu re su
savings banking credit = su ka mi
rural banking secure = lu vo ka
access credit secure = re mi vo
savings rural secure = vo lu su
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: mi. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: savings = su, rural = lu, access = re, banking = ka, credit = mi, secure = vo.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 65 km east, turns left and walks 68 km, then turns left and walks 14 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 85. Net displacement is 51 km east and 68 km north. By Pythagoras, √(51² + 68²) = 85 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 67 km east, turns left and walks 76 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 95. Net displacement is 57 km east and 76 km north. By Pythagoras, √(57² + 76²) = 95 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 41 km east, turns left and walks 28 km, then turns left and walks 20 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. Net displacement is 21 km east and 28 km north. By Pythagoras, √(21² + 28²) = 35 km.

questions.stem: A is the mother of H. B is the daughter of H. E is the father of H. How is B related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. E is a parent of H, and B is H’s daughter. Hence B is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the brother of H. H is the mother of C. G is the father of E and H. How is E related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of C’s mother H. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: G is the only daughter of H. H is the father of G. A is the son of G. E is the sister of H. How is H related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. H is the father of G, and G is A’s mother. Thus H is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 43 candidates, a candidate is 19th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 22. New front rank = 19+3 = 22. Back rank = 43 − 22 + 1 = 22.

questions.stem: In a queue of 62 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. New front rank = 17+4 = 21. Back rank = 62 − 21 + 1 = 42.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹3200 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 6115.56. Recover each cost separately: 3200×100/125 + 3200×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 64 and 96 hours. An outlet empties it in 96 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 64. Net rate = 1/64 + 1/96 − 1/96 = 1/64. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 92 km in still water in 4 hours. If the stream flows at 5 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. Still-water speed = 23 km/h. Upstream speed = 23 − 5. Distance = speed × 2.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 5:3. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 4 months. A receives ₹96000 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 115200. Profit ratio is 60:12. Each ratio unit = ₹1600. Total = 72 × 1600.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹23000 earns ₹6900 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27830. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 10%. Compound amount = 23000 × (1 + 10/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 140 litres of pure milk. 28 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 89.6. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 140 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 29 people is 26 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 56. New total minus old total = (29+1)×(26+1) − 29×26 = 56.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 12 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+12)/(x+12) = 3/2 gives x = 12. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 220 m train moving at 72 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 7.2 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 12.22. Relative speed = (72 − 7.2) ×5/18 = 18 m/s. Time = 220/18.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3000. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.
